key_insight: Bosonic cyclic codes trade a small amount of loss-detection capability for many passive Gaussian logical phase gates, extending rotation-symmetric bosonic codes into a more gate-controllable error-correcting family.
engineering_relevance: This provides a hardware-efficient route to combine quantum error protection with native logical gate implementation, reducing reliance on nonlinear control for bosonic qubits.
method: Generalize rotation-symmetric bosonic codes into cyclic codes with tunable symmetry order.
Convert some higher-order stabilizers into usable logical phase gates via passive Gaussian rotations.
Instantiate the framework with cyclic cat and Vandermonde code families, plus new protocols and gate constructions.
evidence_signal: The abstract reports that sacrificing detectability of a single photon loss can unlock a number of logical phase gates comparable to the code’s original rotation symmetry order, with many desirable code properties preserved.
watch_item: The main tradeoff is reduced error-detection strength relative to the parent rotation-symmetric code, so implementation must balance gate access against loss robustness.
paper_title: Bosonic Cyclic Codes: Trading Stabilizers for Gaussian Non-Clifford Phase Gates
